message.reasoning_content:
Key bugs: parse_u64 sets out=0 first, violating "out unchanged on failure" (e.g. "12x" or empty). Also overflow: out*10 wraps silently, accepts values > UINT64_MAX (e.g. "99999999999999999999" returns wrapped value, contract says reject). Also empty string accepted (contract: nonempty only) — returns true with out=0. Also noexcept but overflow check fine. Registry: get returns string_view into vector while holding lock then releasing — readers may retain view while writers push_back causing reallocation → dangling view. Also get(i) no bounds check (out of range UB). Also add may reallocate while readers hold views — same. Also get returns view after lock released; vector push_back may move → dangling. Fix: return std::string (copy) or keep shared snapshot; bounds check.

Minimal examples:
1. parse_u64("12x", out) with out=5 → returns false but out=0 (changed). Contract violation.
2. parse_u64("", out) → true, out=0 (empty accepted, contract says nonempty).
3. parse_u64("18446744073709551616", out) → true, wraps to 0 (overflow not rejected).
4. Registry: reader holds view from get(0), writer add triggers push_back reallocation → view dangles.
5. get(i) with i >= names.size() → UB (no bounds check).

Fixes: parse_u64: check empty, accumulate into separate variable, only assign out on success, detect overflow via out > (UINT64_MAX - d)/10. Registry: return std::string (copy) or use deque/linked list of immutable blocks; bounds check.

Corrected parse_u64 in cpp block. Keep concise.
